context: Real-time streaming line chart of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with a 60-second main view and 5-minute LTTB-downsampled overview with brush selection, canvas rendering, crosshair, and live stats.
first_impression: A technically impressive real-time chart with data-driven scales and good interaction, undercut by an area fill whose baseline is anchored to the chart bottom rather than zero.
what_works: Y and X domains are fully data-driven (d3.min/max of visible points with symmetric padding), so axes scale correctly with data; LTTB downsampling in the overview is perceptually honest and preserves extrema.
what_doesnt: The area fill is drawn from each data point down to canvas-bottom (y=h), which maps to vMin−pad in data space rather than zero, so the shaded region encodes 'distance from current minimum' not magnitude from a meaningful baseline — a truncated-baseline violation for area fills; no line.defined() guard exists, though the data source has no gaps so it is dormant rather than actively wrong.
